stages.name: Disadvantages of a maximum wage
stages.title: Disadvantages of a maximum wage
stages.sub: Explain why capping pay at the top can backfire for firms and regulators.

steps.q: Becoming a surgeon means years of extra study and training instead of earning a full wage straight away. If the cap means her final pay can never rise much above a nurse's, was that time spent training worth giving up?
steps.right: No, the years given up are wasted for little extra pay
steps.wrong: Yes, the years given up are still worth it
steps.hint: Think about what she gave up by training rather than working, compared with what she now gets back.

steps.q: Knowing that extra training barely raises her pay once capped, is she as keen to take on that training as before?
steps.hint: If the reward for the sacrifice has shrunk, does the sacrifice still feel worth making?

steps.q: A firm's boss is capped at a maximum salary. The law stops the firm paying more in wages, but can it still hand her shares in the company or cover her car and holidays?
steps.hint: The law caps the wage itself. Does it mention every other form of reward a firm could give?

steps.q: If total reward can keep rising through shares, bonuses and perks even though the wage is capped, has the cap really limited what top earners take home?
steps.right: No, firms can get round it
steps.wrong: Yes, it still limits total reward
steps.hint: The wage is only one part of what someone actually receives from the firm.

steps.q: A regulator has to check the pay, bonuses and perks of every top earner across thousands of firms, and work out the exact right cap for each different industry. Is this a quick, cheap job?
steps.right: No, it takes a lot of resources
steps.wrong: Yes, it is quick and cheap
steps.hint: Think about how many firms and pay packages would need checking, and how the right cap could differ by job.
